abi_mismatch_real_fix.what_was_added: tools/xeno_diagnostic_specialist_wrapper_v1.py now has decode_atom_family(atom) plus FAMILY_ORDINAL_RANGES / FAMILY_CLASS_WORDS, both extracted directly from a fresh per-family scan of the real target field of all 16 B0-B6 training files (not guessed, not reused from memory of the earlier flat-vocabulary scan). A validated atom is no longer just 'valid/invalid' -- it is now typed (ORDINAL or CLASS_WORD) and attributed to every trained family whose real observed range/word-set it is consistent with (lists multiple families honestly where the real data is genuinely ambiguous, e.g. ordinals 0-14 are shared by five families; P/Q/R are shared by two GWT families -- not force-picking one).
abi_mismatch_real_fix.honest_limit_not_worked_around: This solves the ENGINEERING half of the ABI mismatch (bare string -> typed, family-attributable structure). It does not and cannot solve the DATA half: the diagnostic model was trained on placeholder ABI_ACCEPTED_ORDINAL:NN atoms, not the real tokenizer-bound 46-symbol production alphabet from XENO_SHELL_MASTER_SPEC.md SS7. Closing that gap requires retraining on real-ABI-bound data (atoms_index.json, real token IDs) -- a new training pass, which was neither authorized (the one paid Together run already happened, 'EIN Lauf' was explicit) nor attempted here. Reported as BLOCKED-BY-DATA, not silently bypassed.
abi_mismatch_real_fix.tests_added: 8 new offline tests (test_decode_ordinal_single_family, test_decode_ordinal_ambiguous_shared_range, test_decode_ordinal_b5_range, test_decode_class_word_single_family, test_decode_class_word_shared_between_two_gwt_families, test_decode_real_holdout_hits_from_the_live_sandbox_demo, test_wrap_includes_family_decode_when_valid, test_wrap_family_decode_is_none_when_rejected) -- 22 total in the file now, all passing. Also reran tests/test_xeno_shell_packets_v1.py and tests/test_xeno_shell_s0s1s2_transitions_v1.py: 41 tests total across all three files, all green, no regressions.

core_integration_status: The 0.8B core (huihui-ai/Huihui-Qwen3.5-0.8B-abliterated base + the actual Together LoRA adapter from job ft-959a53c0-8228) is the load-bearing model behind load_diagnostic_model()/generate_and_validate() -- this is not a placeholder or mock, it is the real trained artifact, confirmed by matching raw generations against the original holdout test byte-for-byte on overlapping rows.

extended_real_test.why_bigger: Original demonstration used the same 12 rows as the initial holdout test. This run uses 48 FRESH real HOLDOUT_FROZEN rows (3 per family across all 16 trained families, sampled with a different random seed, never seen in training), run live in the claylab sandbox through the extended wrapper.

results.shell_validation_rate: 62.5% (30/48) -- well-formed trained atoms, correct or not
results.exact_task_accuracy: 27.1% (13/48) -- up from the original 12-row sample's 16.7%; larger sample gives a more stable, still honest, still modest estimate. Not framed as a success -- most validated atoms were still the wrong specific answer.

extended_real_test.new_finding_from_the_family_decode_layer: The typed decode surfaced a failure category the original binary shell check could not see: real cross-family confusion. 4 of the 48 rows (all from B2_MID_EPISODE_REMAP or B2_PRIOR_OVERRIDE, both of which expect an ABI_ACCEPTED_ORDINAL answer) instead produced ALLOW/ABSTAIN -- real trained atoms, but ones that only belong to the unrelated B0_READ family. Plausible cause: B2 prompts contain literal 'ALLOW=>...', 'DENY=>...', 'ABSTAIN=>...' codebook-key text as part of the prompt surface, and the model sometimes echoes one of those keys instead of dereferencing to the mapped ordinal value -- a second, distinct confusion pattern from the B3 code-derailment one, not previously visible in the smaller 12-row sample or the plain accept/reject check.
